facts.fact: The terms of reference of February 2024 state that the registration of civil-status events in Djibouti-Ville (births, civil and religious marriages, divorces and deaths) is done by the civil-status centres and has rested since 2011 on software for entering, transmitting and using the data, the maternity antennas entering birth declarations in the system and the central centre drawing up death and marriage acts.

The terms of reference of February 2024 state that civil-status antennas inside maternities enter birth declarations in the system, that the database has been fed continuously since 2011 by the entries of civil-status agents, and that the data sit on a central server in a room of the Hôtel de Ville; the system is the city's, and the document does not say it is held in a national register.

The terms of reference of February 2024 list the city's civil-status sites as the Mairie's central centre, three commune centres (one per commune) and five antennas in maternities (four at Balbala, one at Boulaos), nine in all; they cover Djibouti-Ville only, give no national count of offices, and set the diagnostic to study extending the system for better coverage of the city.

The terms of reference of February 2024 state that the Ville de Djibouti has held the civil-status service since the Ministry of the Interior transferred the competence in 2008 and that its communes have exercised it since SIGEC became operational in 2011, on means that are insufficient but dedicated; the software was developed by the firm SDSI and the system's administrator is a former technician of that firm.

The terms of reference of February 2024 place the SIGEC diagnostic and its budgeted action plan under component 1 of PROGOUV, a EUR 8 million governance support project for the Ville de Djibouti carried out with Expertise France's technical assistance; the city's own means for civil status are called insufficient but dedicated, and no domestic budget line is stated.

systems.country_label: système informatisé de gestion de l'état civil (SIGEC) de la Ville de Djibouti
systems.platform: software developed by the Société de Développement des Systèmes d'Information (SDSI); central server at the Hôtel de Ville
systems.owner: Ville de Djibouti (Mairie, maître d'ouvrage); exercised by the communes
systems.tiers: Djibouti-Ville: the central civil-status centre, three commune centres and five maternity antennas (Cheikho hospital, PK12 polyclinic, Al-Rahma, Hayableh, Dar El-Hanan hospital), since 2011
most of the central centre's large, old archive was scanned and indexed when the system was set up in 2011
